I am currently a Ph.D. candidate in Political Science at the University of Texas at Dallas. My research interests include civil resistance, democratic backsliding, elections and voting behavior, and East Asian politics.
My research examines various aspects of protests and social movements. I am currently studying the role of diaspora organizations in shaping democratic support for pro-democracy protests. My ongoing research also compares the political participation and attitudes of citizens in Hong Kong and Taiwan using election and survey data. My findings have been presented at academic conferences, including the American Political Science Association and the Midwest Political Science Association. My work has been published in the Journal of Peace Research, Issues & Studies, and the Journal of Asian and African Studies.
My teaching experience includes courses on protests and social movements, Chinese and Taiwanese politics, and introductory research design.
